analysis: The supplied units are head-side excerpts of desktop-app/package-lock.json, lines 4706-6238. The patch excerpt is truncated and the range map is complete. The changes are dev-dependency bumps: electron 44.5.1 to 44.9.1, vite 8.3.2 to 8.3.5, rolldown 1.2.12 to 1.2.15, @oxc-project/types 0.152 to 0.155, plus new lightningcss and rolldown binding entries and the removal of roarr's old sub-dependencies. In the visible excerpts every package has a registry.npmjs.org resolved URL and a sha512 integrity hash. I saw no git, file or http dependency, and no alternate-registry URL. I saw no integrity removed or downgraded, and no install scripts added. Packages in the excerpt that are flagged "dev" (rolldown at 5998, postcss, sharp, node-gyp) are build-time only. react, react-dom and lucide-react are runtime and unchanged in my view. The lockfile touches no provider code, no coordinator WebSocket contract, no attestation, no key custody and no cache storage. It therefore does not affect TB-011, T-009, T-013, T-036 or the other retained entries. Coverage limits: I could not see the changed hunks elsewhere in the file (lines 24-2018 and 6590+), nor the electron entry itself. I did not verify that the integrity hashes match the registry, or whether electron 44.9.1 carries a vulnerability or a fix. Those are supply-chain facts outside the supplied evidence, so I record them here and raise no finding. Electron is the shipped desktop shell, so the integration pass should check its resolved URL and integrity if that hunk is in scope. There is no provider attack-surface change in this unit.
